$comment: What has actually been READ by a named role, as opposed to what a gate asserts. scripts/check-review-coverage.mjs prints the percentage on every run and fails only on incoherence — a claim naming a path that does not exist, or a claim with no reviewer, date or depth. Seeded honestly on 2026-08-19: the number is small on purpose, because the alternative was leaving it invisible. depth: read = opened and understood; audited = read adversarially against a specific question; verified-live = checked against a real running system.

Checked field by field against real FreeRADIUS. quarantined is never a wire fact; lastAuthAt is not an authentication fact.
Ladder rungs driven individually; an egress proxy collapses dns_failing.
Against a real TLS-intercepting gateway; interception is observable via the certificate issuer, so service_observing_traffic need not be a self-report.
Vendor documentation confirms its refusal to infer auth state from the endpoint resource. NOT verified against an instance.
HeadwindLabDevice checked against a real Headwind CE 5.30.3 over the launcher wire protocol.
Role/permission table — found tenant:admin granted and required by nothing.
IPv6 fallback keyed raw addresses; now subnet-bucketed via the library key generator.
Full site sweep: 14 findings, 8 applied — router-base 404s, invisible signal dots, contrast, reduced motion, worker-PWA claims.
All 15 workflows: permissions, injection, action pinning, timeouts, concurrency, and the SBOM token split.
Found it path-filtered away from the Kotlin client it exists to bind.
Every cited file and command resolved; both load-bearing claims checked against the code. Accurate.

Every path and every per-operation security declaration read against the served routers. info.description asserted every route derives its tenant from the bearer token; 21 of 55 documented operations carry no principal at all. Nothing said the /cp/v1 surface and GET /v1/keys are registered only under the review-demo profile.

Read only routes/v1.ts and skipped /cp/v1 by design, so 21 documented control-plane operations were ungated and three served routes had drifted out of the spec while it printed 'Contract holds'. Widened to the whole served surface; self-test 7/7.
Router composition and the demo-profile fence. The reasoning for not mounting rather than 403'ing is sound and written down; it had simply never reached the published contract.
Postman-drift branch kept only the LAST line of the checker's output, so a multi-line failure reported an empty reason. Fixed and verified with an induced drift.
The collection is hand-authored and checked against the spec, not generated from it — so a new spec path needs a matching item added by hand.

Driven against a real Postgres ledger: clean, mid-chain tamper (localised to the exact index, exit 1), and end-truncation (Chain intact, exit 0). Refused a missing DATABASE_URL as an unearned affirmative while exiting 0 on an empty table; --min-records added.
14/14 on real Postgres. Added the end-truncation limit as a passing assertion so it fails the day an anchor is added; both new assertions confirmed to fail when the deletion is removed.

16/16 on real Postgres. Refutes the roster claim that the restore path was only described — flipped byte, truncated archive and missing manifest all refused, and a good archive accepted as the negative control.
Accurate on backup/restore/refusals. Said nothing about deletion from the end leaving verification clean; that section added.
verifySegment recomputes body-plus-prevHash per record and checks the prevHash link separately, so an edit is caught two ways. Neither way can see a missing tail.

Read field by field against a live Keycloak 26.4. assurance, freshness and binding are none of them wire facts: no amr anywhere, no auth_time, token exp 60s vs session max 36000s, and no device field in the session record. The type's own comment already says it consumes an evaluated view, which is what makes it correct.
Normalizes report.freshness through oneOf with an unknown fallback rather than deriving it from a token — the one place the exp trap could have entered, and it does not.
Every unknown raises the bar; a mismatched subject on a live session is the strongest negative. Fail-closed law holds under all three unknowns the wire actually produces.
14/14 against a live Keycloak 26.4, including cross-implementation RFC 7638 thumbprint agreement and rejections asserted to be for their own reason rather than a key-loading failure.
Accurate, but describes the client setup in prose only; following it produced a 13/14 on a misread mapper claim value. A setup script would not have made the mistake.

Read against the fail-closed invariant after the sweep's counterexample. Both grant exits returned none whether or not nacCompliant and freshness were reported — unknown graded identical to known-good. Fixed: verified-good none, unreported monitor (AUTHENTICATED_POSTURE_UNVERIFIED), reported-bad step_up. Negative control confirmed the new checks fail on the old code.

riskState unknown + riskLevel unknown + zero detections graded trusted/NO_RISK/none, and the normalizer had no arm for Entra's clean value 'none' — so parse failure and a clean tenant were the same state, graded trusted. Fixed both halves together; a real detection still outranks the new monitor floor.
normalizeRiskState default arm swallowed the most common healthy-tenant value. Vendor 'none' now maps to riskState 'none'; unmapped values still fall to 'unknown', which no longer earns trust.
The shared enumeration harness read end to end before extending its reach — self-proof carries both too-strict and too-loose negative controls, so a predicate error in either direction is caught.
Already fully enumerated by hand (360 combinations, granting set pinned by equality) — the symbol-grep coverage count under-reported it. The launch family is covered.

Shift-1 sweep: found wedge #14 — a finding whose severity failed to parse fell to the low/info residual and graded low_risk/LOW_SEVERITY_ONLY. Now unknown/SEVERITY_UNVERIFIED/monitor; grant pinned by enumeration to the attested-empty scan only.

Coverage audit: already fully enumerated by hand (2160 states, granting set pinned exactly, ZERO unjustified grants). Counted toward the shift-1 covered tier without modification — symbol-grep undercounts hand-rolled sweeps.

Shift-1 sweep: wedges #12/#13 — unknown freshness (null/unparseable capturedAt) skipped the stale guard and granted on_premises; a future-dated capture read as fresh. Both now UNVERIFIED_LOCATION_FRESHNESS/monitor; enumeration pins the single granting state.

Shift-2 role split, proven on real Postgres 16: runtime holds SELECT+INSERT on the ledger (append-only by privilege), SELECT+INSERT+UPDATE on upserting stores, no DDL/DELETE/TRUNCATE; SQL is idempotent and doubles as the post-restore re-provisioning step. Fail-closed after Codex review: refuses to ADOPT a preexisting elevated/owning/member role, and assertRoleSplitProvisionable refuses migrations/restores up front when the role is missing and the credential lacks CREATEROLE.

Executed against a local PostgreSQL 16 before CI: 61/61, three consecutive runs (idempotent from a used cluster). Positive direction, seven denial classes (all 42501), admin non-vacuity, the backup → posture-destroyed → restore round trip, and the Codex-review guard set: migrations/restore refuse UP FRONT without CREATEROLE (database untouched, proven by row counts), the split refuses to adopt a preexisting SUPERUSER/owning/member role, all three durable components (decision, session, ledger) refuse readiness on missing grants; PUBLIC/column/sequence/schema/database grant wedges staged and proven converged; owner-rights paths (SECURITY DEFINER routines, writable views) staged and REFUSED until the administrator locks them down; partial connection caps, non-relation ownership, SECURITY DEFINER triggers, rewrite rules, and PUBLIC-inherited schema CREATE refused; bare-database apply proven (guarded relation lookups); forbidden-privilege readiness (negative probe) proven; restore re-locks archived definer routines (pg_restore default-ACL artifact); grants outside the canonical set refused (pg_shdepend allowlist) staged and proven converged; NOLOGIN, CONNECTION LIMIT 0, expired VALID UNTIL, schema/database ownership, and cross-database ownership (pg_shdepend) refused; db:migrate proven as the repair command on an already-current database; runtime connects via its direct CONNECT grant on a hardened cluster; a restore credential without grant authority (owns tables, not the database) is refused before pg_restore, and role loss recovers to the same posture. Destructive runs are gated behind SIGNALGRID_DB_DISPOSABLE=1 (loud refusal, never a silent skip).

The disposable-cluster declaration (SIGNALGRID_DB_DISPOSABLE=1) every destructive Postgres proof now requires. DATABASE_URL alone is not consent: the proofs DROP the tables they test and the role-split proof re-passwords the cluster-wide runtime role. Refusal is exit 1 and loud — a silent skip in CI would leave the gate green while testing nothing. Refusal path executed locally.

Prototype-key outcomes passed `in OUTCOME_RANK` and stuck as the reduce accumulator (rank undefined loses every > as NaN), erasing a genuine deny and making the answer order-dependent — falsifying the module's own headline law. FIXED: Set membership in validateRecord and in the exported mostRestrictiveOutcome. Also read: the standing bound cannot expire an ONLINE record (continuity.ts:276) — tested and intended, recorded so nobody re-finds it as a bug.

Per-signal `freshness` is computed and stamped by dock.ts but buildEvidence never reads it — only category/value/observedAt. A year-old tamper_state:'none' is indistinguishable from a fresh one, and a dock that honestly reports sensor_unavailable steps up while a silent dock does not. OPEN, not fixed here. Also: deriveCriticalSignalsPresent omits osSupported and counts postureFreshness 'expired' as present.

Validates authored rules at the write boundary, then most-restrictive-wins with a step_up default and an allow-on-degraded backstop. The backstop's critical set is five fields; shipped v1 rules mask the osSupported gap, but createPolicyDraft can activate a rule set that does not.
Tenant-safe facade: every method resolves a bearer token to a principal and checks one named Permission before any query; no method takes a caller-supplied tenant id. No fail-closed inversion found.
The decision loop — resolve, gather, derive, evaluate, snapshot, persist, audit, remediate, webhook. No fail-closed inversion found.

Turns reason codes into ordered routed steps and can project a re-evaluation. Three fields written and never read: summaryForOperator, projectedReasonCodes, clears — while the sibling summaryForWorker IS rendered twice.

The remediation allow (lines 220-227) does not carry the `outcomes.size === 0` guard the base allow requires, so remediation.verified plus a non-suppressing outcome (api.integration_failed, low_battery, health_degraded) yields allow where the same evidence without it does not. OPEN — deliberately not fixed: this file is the byte-faithful source of the Swift port and changing it breaks parity. Also confirmed: SignalGridDecision.confidence has zero readers anywhere.
Strongest action wins, tier follows, drivers most-severe-first. Zero signals compose to ok/none — handled downstream by signalCount and pinned by two proofs, so not a defect.

40 one-line mappings plus fromDevicePosture, the only one with real logic (13 conditions over five Graph fields; 3 of 900 input states grant). All 40 cast recommendedAction with no runtime check — every member is on the ladder today, so safe by construction, but it is a load-bearing invariant with no guard.

Read in full, 47 lines. Two findings. (1) `nginx_certs` is mounted at /etc/nginx/certs by docker-compose.yml and NOTHING reads it — the config has `listen 80` only and no ssl_certificate directive. A TLS volume wired in and consumed by nothing is the same shape as the tenant:admin precedent this repo was founded on: a control that reads as protection and is not. (2) X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-For are set only on /api/; /app/ and / set X-Real-IP alone, so the app behind them cannot learn the original scheme. Both are LOCAL-STACK ONLY — prod does not run nginx at all, which is finding 3 in backlog row 64 and matters more than either.

Local stack: api + web + nginx, and NO database. Mounts nginx.conf read-only, plus an nginx_certs volume nothing consumes. Compared against docker-compose.prod.yml, which is db + api with no web tier and no proxy — the two stacks are not the same product.

Prod stack: db + api only. The API is exposed DIRECTLY on 8080 with no reverse proxy — zero nginx mentions in the file. db has a healthcheck and api waits on it. So every routing, path-prefix and forwarded-header behaviour exercised through the local nginx tier is absent in production, and docs/RUN_AND_GO_LIVE.md never mentions nginx either.

Read end to end earlier this session for the corepack/CVE work. npm and the corepack cache are removed from the shipping image with a build-time assertion. Finding recorded as row 59: `corepack enable pnpm` runs in BOTH stages, so each build makes an un-retried network fetch of pnpm from registry.npmjs.org; one of them died mid-download on 2026-08-24 (undici assert(!this.paused)) and failed the job. The obvious fix — carry the builder's corepack cache forward — is exactly what lines 97-111 deliberately strip for CVE reasons, so it needs a retry, not a cache.

Read end to end. The live-call gate for the emitter family. Strongest property in the family: ItsmFixtureRecord types `delivered` as the literal `false` and `mode` as the literal "fixture", so a fixture record that claims delivery is UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely absent — the syslog family's status:'sent' lie cannot recur here by construction. ItsmFixtureEmitter is deterministic: no clock, no randomness, seq derived from log length. No live transport ships in this repository, so the live path's failure mode is 'there is no code'.

Read end to end (10 lines). Re-exports ./resolve and ./adapter, and via adapter.ts re-exports all eight vendor adapter CLASSES as public surface. Checked the bypass this implies: no call site outside the itsm module constructs an adapter directly (only dist/ build output matches), and each vendor file carries its own resolveEmission() check on its emit path (3-6 sites each), so the factory tier gate is defence in depth rather than the only door. Pulling that thread found the check-ungated-fetch scope defect fixed in this commit (backlog row 65).
